title: AI Foundations Capstone
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to determine whether available evidence supports a source-driven correction and to identify the evidence still needed when the affected learning content is UNKNOWN.
objectives: Determine whether the supplied evidence establishes that a cited source moved or passed its review cadence.
Identify the source records and baseline content needed to make a source-driven correction without changing unaffected material.
Check that knowledge-check answer indexes refer to valid zero-based positions in their choice arrays.

sections.title: Correction status
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level review of the requested source correction. The exact existing module content is absent, including its instructional claims, questions, source records, review cadence, and previous verification date.

Which cited source changed is UNKNOWN. The supplied record identifies only the target file and describes its publisher as unregistered and its verification status as never verified. It does not provide the previous source URL, a replacement URL, or evidence that a replacement is the authoritative continuation of the previous source.

What the source change affected is also UNKNOWN. Establishing the effect requires comparing the existing module, the former source, and the current authoritative source. Because those materials are absent, no particular claim, answer, explanation, objective, estimate, or provider declaration can be corrected from the supplied evidence.
sections.callout: No source-driven content correction can be established until the previous source, the current authoritative source, and the exact baseline module are available.

sections.title: Evidence required for a minimal change
paragraphs: A source move can be established by obtaining the previous URL, the replacement URL, and evidence that the replacement is the authoritative continuation of the previous source. A review-cadence trigger can be evaluated only when the prior verification date and review-cadence interval are available.

Leaving unaffected material unchanged requires the exact committed baseline. Without that baseline, a comparison cannot distinguish an established correction from a rewrite. Catalogue-wide identifier uniqueness and prerequisite resolution also remain UNKNOWN because the catalogue registry was not supplied.
Direct HTTPS resolution of the sources could not be tested because network retrieval was unavailable on 2026-08-21. Their retrieval status is therefore CANNOT VERIFY, not disproved.

sections.title: JSON validation concepts
paragraphs: JSON defines an object as an unordered collection of name-value pairs and an array as an ordered sequence of values. A top-level object is enclosed by opening and closing braces.
JSON.parse processes a JSON text and returns its represented value. Text that does not follow the JSON grammar produces a syntax error.
The answerIndex values in this module use zero-based indexing. An answerIndex of 0 selects the first choice, 1 selects the second choice, and 2 selects the third choice.

questions.prompt: What does the supplied evidence establish about which cited source changed and what content it affected?
choices: It establishes both the replacement source and every affected paragraph.
It establishes that the source passed its review cadence.
The changed source and its effects are UNKNOWN because the necessary source records and baseline content are absent.
questions.explanation: The module states that the previous URL, replacement URL, review metadata, authoritative-continuation evidence, and baseline module are absent. The changed source and its effects therefore remain UNKNOWN.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is needed to establish that a source moved?
choices: Only the target module file name.
The previous URL, the replacement URL, and evidence that the replacement is the authoritative continuation.
Only a new title for the module.
questions.explanation: The minimal-change section identifies the previous URL, replacement URL, and authoritative-continuation evidence as the information needed to establish a source move.

questions.prompt: Which choice does an answerIndex of 0 select?
choices: The final choice regardless of array length.
questions.explanation: The module explains that zero-based indexing assigns position 0 to the first array element.
